paraphrase: The difficulty of finding the freedoms and advantages: a human life free of the eight unfree states and endowed with the ten advantages (five personal, five circumstantial) is rarer than a turtle putting its head through a yoke on the ocean; it is also threatened by the eight intrusive circumstances and eight incompatible propensities.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: The impermanence of life: the outer universe, the beings in it, even holy beings and the buddhas pass away; the circumstances of death are countless and the time uncertain; so one should practise now.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: The defects of saṃsāra: the sufferings of the hells, the hungry spirits, the animals, humans (birth, ageing, sickness, death and more), the demigods and the gods — there is no place in saṃsāra beyond suffering.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: Actions, cause and effect: the ten non-virtuous actions and their fully ripened effect, the effect similar to the cause (in experience and in tendency) and the conditioning effect; the ten virtues to be adopted; the smallest act is not wasted.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: The benefits of liberation: only liberation and omniscience are free of suffering; the aspiration for them is roused by the preceding contemplations.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: How to follow a spiritual teacher: examine the teacher first (pure vows, learning, compassion, experience of the practice, freedom from worldly aims), rather than taking anyone because of fame; then follow him with faith and service, and emulate his realization and conduct; false teachers are compared to a millstone tied around the neck.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: Taking refuge: the refuge of faith in the Three Jewels, and in the Three Roots (guru, yidam, ḍākinī) and in the channels, winds and essences and the nature of mind, visualized as the refuge tree; with prostrations; and the precepts of refuge (what to avoid, what to do, and additional practices).
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: Arousing bodhicitta: training in the four boundless attitudes, then the aspiring and applying bodhicitta, equalizing and exchanging oneself and others and taking on others' suffering; the precepts of the bodhisattva.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: Meditation and recitation of Vajrasattva to purify wrongdoing and obscurations, complete with the four powers: the power of the support, of regret, of resolution, and of the antidote (the visualization and the hundred-syllable mantra).
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: The maṇḍala offering to gather the two accumulations of merit and wisdom: offering the universe and all one's wealth and merit to the Three Jewels.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: The kusāli's accumulation: the renunciant's offering of his own body, visualized as cut up and transformed into nectar for the guests of the four kinds, cutting attachment to the body.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: Guru yoga, the ultimate method for arousing wisdom: visualizing the guru as Padmasambhava, supplicating him with the Seven-line prayer and the Vajra Guru mantra, receiving the four empowerments and mixing one's mind with his; devotion is said to be the only cause of the realization of the natural state.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).

paraphrase: Transference of consciousness (phowa), 'buddhahood without meditation', is taught as an auxiliary. Of its kinds (dharmakāya, sambhogakāya, nirmāṇakāya, the ordinary transference with three recognitions, and the transference for the dead by the hook of compassion), only the ordinary one is practised in training, and never applied before the signs of death are complete: to transfer untimely is like killing the deities.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase). RESTRICTED: classification and the text's warning only; no method recorded.

paraphrase: How to listen: avoid the three defects of the vessel (an upturned pot that hears nothing, a leaking pot that forgets, a pot with poison that mixes the teaching with bad motives) and the six stains (pride, lack of faith, lack of interest, outward distraction, inward tension, weariness); listen with the vast attitude of bodhicitta and the skilful attitude of secret mantra, seeing teacher, place and teaching as pure.
speaker: Patrul Rinpoche (recording Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu)
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase).
